newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain accepts private assets as collateral.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain accepts private assets as collateral.

text.p: Spanish central bank general director Gonzalo Gil said on Thursday that private assets will be admitted from today as collateral for repurchase agreements with the Bank of Spain.
"Starting from today, we can use private assets, shares and fixed-income, " Gonzalo Gil told an Intermoney seminar.
The new facility, which the Bank of Spain announced last December, must fulfil the following requirements:
Fixed-income assets must be denominated in pesetas, with a minimum outstanding five billion pesetas in the issue and a remaining life of at least three months.
Shares must be in the index of the most liquid Ibex-35, but may not be of banks, and may not be issues from the group which is presenting them as collateral.
The maximum value admitted will be 50 percent of their value, calculated at market prices.
Gil added that the Bank of Spain is also starting to move from a system of gross clearing made at the end of the day toward a new system which will take place throughout the day.
He added that these changes are required by the preparation to be part of Europe's single currency.
